Rashi on Nedarim 2a:1:1.hebrew: כל כנויי נדרים כנדרים - דעיקר נדר דכתיב בתורה (במדבר ל׳:ג׳) "איש כי ידור נדר", דאמר: "קרבן שאני אוכל לך", או "קרבן שאני נהנה לך". ואם אמר בלשון אחר, בכינוי נדר, כדקתני לקמן: "קונם שאני נהנה לך", או "קונם שאיני נהנה לך" — דאם כינה לקרבן בהני לשונות, נמי מיתסר בהו בנדרים, כמו שאסור גבי קרבן. וכן "כנויי חרמים כחרמים", וכן "כנויי שבועות" כו' — מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Nedarim 2a:1:1.english: All substitutes for vows are like vows - For the primary [form of a] vow written in the Torah (Numbers 30:3), "When a man vows a vow," [is] when one says: "[That which] I eat of yours [shall be forbidden to me as] an offering," or "[That which] I benefit from you [shall be forbidden to me as] an offering." And if he spoke in another phrasing, using a substitute [term] for a vow, as [the Mishnah] teaches below: "Konam [that which] I benefit from you," or "Konam that I will not benefit from you" — for if he substituted [a term] for an offering with these expressions, [the benefit] is also forbidden to him through them by [the laws of] vows, just as it is forbidden with regard to an offering. And similarly, "The substitutes for devotions are like devotions," and similarly, "The substitutes for oaths..." etc. — [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Nedarim 2a:3:1.hebrew: מודר אני ממך - כלומר: ״הרי עלי כנדר מה שאני נהנה ממך״, או א"ל ״מופרשני ממך״ בהאי לשון, או אמר ״מרוחק אני ממך״ — דמשמע דמיתסר נפשיה ולא מיתהני מיניה. וכל הני, כיון דלא מפרש ממש לנדר, דלא מידכר ביה שום לשון קרבן — הויין ידות:
Rashi on Nedarim 2a:3:1.english: I am avowed from you - That is to say: "Whatever benefit I derive from you is upon me like a vow"; or if he said to him, "I am separated from you," using this phrasing; or if he said, "I am distanced from you" — which implies that he forbids himself and does not derive benefit from him. And all these, since he did not explicitly articulate an actual vow, as no term of an offering is mentioned in it, are intimations [of vows].

Rashi on Nedarim 2a:4:1.hebrew: מנודה אני לך - כמו שאם היה בנידוי, דאסור ליה לישא וליתן בהדיה — כך אסר נפשיה עליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 2a:4:1.english: I am ostracized from you - Just as if he were under a ban of excommunication, where it is forbidden to engage in business with him, so he forbade himself from him.

Rashi on Nedarim 2a:4:2.hebrew: ר"ע היה חוכך בזה להחמיר - הוה מחכך להחמיר דאסור נמי, דענין נדר הוא; ולא בריר ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 2a:4:2.english: Rabbi Akiva was deliberating about this to rule stringently - He was deliberating [whether] to rule stringently, that [it is] also forbidden, for it is a matter of a vow; but it was not clear to him.

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:1.hebrew: מנודה אני לך - כלומר, כמנודה שאסור לההנותו, כך אהא אסור ליהנות ממך:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:1.english: I am ostracized from you - That is to say: Just as with an ostracized person, whom it is forbidden to benefit, so shall I be forbidden to derive benefit from you.

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:2.hebrew: ר׳ עקיבא היה חוכך בזה להחמיר - כאדם שמתחכך אילך ואילך, כך איהו לא בריר ליה שיהא ודאי אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:2.english: Rabbi Akiva was inclined to be stringent in this matter - Like a person who rubs himself this way and that way, so it was not clear to him that it is definitely forbidden.

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:1:1.hebrew: כל כנויי נדרים כנדרים וחרמים כחרמים - כינוי — זהו שם שפל (נ"א טפל), כדאמרי': "המכנה שם לחברו". ה"נ כנויי נדרים — דעיקר הנדר הוא כשמתפיס החפץ בדבר הנדור, כמו דאמר: "הרי עלי ככר זה כהקדש", ועל ככר אחר אומר: "יהא כזה" — זהו נדר, כדאמר פרק ג' דשבועות (ד' כ): "עד שידור בדבר הנדור"; והני לישני כעין נדר הן. ולקמן בשילהי פירקין קאמר ר"ל: לשון שבדו חכמי', ולהכי תקינו כנויי — דלא לימא "קרבן לה'", דזימנין דאמר "לה'" ולא אמר "לקרבן", ומפיק שם שמים לבטלה. ור' יוחנן אמר: לשון נכרים, דבלשונם כשנודרין נדר אומרים הכי. וקשה למ"ד לשון נכרים: אמאי נקט הני לישני? לימא: בכל הלשונות שהם נודרים בלשונם יהא נדר! ואומר ר"י: ודאי אם יהא כלשונם יהא נדר, אחרי שהם מבינים; והני דמתני', אפי' לא יבינו האי לשון — הרי הוא נדר. ולמ"ד לשון שבדו חכמים קשה: דה"נ כנויי דנזיר בדו חכמים? והיכי יביא קרבן על לשון חכמים?! ובנדרים לא קשה אי עבר בבל תאחר על לשון חכמים. וי"ל: דהא דאמר ל' בדו, לא קאמר אלא גבי נדרים, אבל לא גבי נזיר. וכן מוכח בגמרא דפריך: "הניחא למ"ד לשון נכרים, אלא למ"ד לשון שבדו חכמים מאי איכא למימר?" ובמס' נזיר דקאמר "כל כנויי נזירות כנזירות", לא פריך כה"ג בגמ'. ואור"י: דאין זו ראיה, דרגילות הוא להאריך במקום אחד ולקצר במקום אחר; ועל לשון שבדו חכמים נמי הוי נזיר, דכיון דתקינו חכמים שנודרין בהני לישני הוי כעיקר נזירות, ויש כח בידיהם לעשות תקנתן כעיקר נזירות. ועוד י"ל: כיון שתיקנו חכמים הני לישני, כוונת הנודר לנדר גמור, וגמר בלבו לעשותו כעיקר הלשון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:1:1.english: All substitutes of vows are like vows, and [substitutes of] devotions are like devotions - A substitute [kinnui] — this is an inferior name (another version: a secondary [name]), as we say: "One who gives a derogatory nickname to his fellow." So too, "substitutes of vows" [are inferior names]: for the primary [form of a] vow is when one associates an item with an object forbidden by a vow — as when one says, "Behold this loaf is upon me like consecrated property," and regarding another loaf he says, "Let it be like this [one]" — this is a vow, as [the Gemara] says in the third chapter of Shevuot (20a): "[A vow does not take effect] until he vows by an object that was already forbidden [by a vow]"; and these expressions [of substitutes] are a semblance of a vow. And later, at the end of our chapter [10a], Reish Lakish says: [They are] language that the Sages invented. And for this reason did they institute substitutes: so that one would not say, "[This is like a] sacrifice to the Lord," for at times he might say "to the Lord" and not say "a sacrifice," and thus utter the Name of Heaven in vain. And Rabbi Yochanan says: [They are] foreign languages, for in their languages, when they make a vow, they say this. And a difficulty arises according to the one who said [they are] foreign languages: Why did [the Mishnah] specify these expressions? Let it say: In all languages that they make vows in their language, let it be a vow! And the Ri says: Certainly, if it is in their language, it will be a vow, since they understand [it]; whereas these [expressions] of the Mishnah, even if they do not understand this language, behold it is a vow. And according to the one who said [they are] language that the Sages invented, a difficulty arises: Did the Sages also invent substitutes for nazirite vows? And how could one bring a sacrificial offering based on language of rabbinic enactment?! And regarding vows it is not difficult whether he violates [the prohibition of] "you shall not delay" based on rabbinic language. And one can answer: That which [Reish Lakish] said, "[It is] language they invented," he said only regarding vows, but not regarding a nazirite. And so it is proven in the Gemara, as it asks [10b]: "This works out well according to the one who said [substitutes are] foreign languages; but according to the one who said [substitutes are] language that the Sages invented, what can be said?" Whereas in Tractate Nazir [2a], where it states: "All substitutes for nazirite vows are like nazirite vows," it does not ask in this manner in the Gemara. And the Ri says: This is no proof, for it is common [for the Talmud] to elaborate in one place and be concise in another place; and based on language that the Sages invented, he also becomes a nazirite, for since the Sages instituted that one may vow with these expressions, it is like essential naziriteship, and they have the authority in their hands to make their enactment like essential naziriteship. And furthermore one can answer: Since the Sages instituted these expressions, the intention of the vower is for a full vow, and he resolved in his heart to make it like the primary language [of the Torah].

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:1:2.hebrew: כל כנויי נדרים כנדרים וחרמים כחרמים - כינוי זהו שם שפל (נ"א טפל), כדאמרי': "המכנה שם לחברו". ה"נ כנויי נדרים — דעיקר הנדר הוא כשמתפיס החפץ בדבר הנדור, כמו דאמר: "הרי עלי ככר זה כהקדש", ועל ככר אחר אומר: "יהא כזה" — זהו נדר, כדאמר פרק ג' דשבועות (ד' כ): "עד שידור בדבר הנדור"; והני לישני כעין נדר הן. ולקמן בשילהי פירקין קאמר ר"ל: "לשון שבדו חכמי'", ולהכי תקינו כנויי — דלא לימא "קרבן לה'", דזימנין דאמר "לה'" ולא אמר "לקרבן", ומפיק שם שמים לבטלה. ור' יוחנן אמר: "לשון נכרים", דבלשונם כשנודרין נדר אומרים הכי. וקשה למ"ד "לשון נכרים": אמאי נקט הני לישני? לימא: "בכל הלשונות שהם נודרים בלשונם יהא נדר"! ואומר ר"י: ודאי אם יהא כלשונם יהא נדר אחרי שהם מבינים; והני דמתני', אפי' לא יבינו האי לשון — הרי הוא נדר. ולמ"ד "לשון שבדו חכמים" קשה: דה"נ כנויי דנזיר בדו חכמים, והיכי יביא קרבן על לשון חכמים? ובנדרים לא קשה אי עבר בבל תאחר על לשון חכמים. וי"ל: דהא דאמר "ל' בדו" לא קאמר אלא גבי נדרים אבל לא גבי נזיר; וכן מוכח בגמרא, דפריך: "הניחא למ"ד לשון נכרים, אלא למ"ד לשון שבדו חכמים מאי איכא למימר?", ובמס' נזיר דקאמר "כל כנויי נזירות כנזירות" לא פריך כה"ג בגמ'. ואור"י: דאין זו ראיה, דרגילות הוא להאריך במקום אחד ולקצר במקום אחר; ועל לשון שבדו חכמים נמי הוי נזיר — דכיון דתקינו חכמים שנודרין בהני לישני הוי כעיקר נזירות, ויש כח בידיהם לעשות תקנתן כעיקר נזירות. ועוד י"ל: כיון שתיקנו חכמים הני לישני, כוונת הנודר לנדר גמור, וגמר בלבו לעשותו כעיקר הלשון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:1:2.english: "All substitutes for vows are like vows, and [substitutes for] bans are like bans" - A substitute [kinui] is a degraded name (a variant reading: a secondary name), as we say: "One who gives a derogatory nickname [hamekhanneh shem] to his fellow." So too here, substitutes for vows [are secondary terms] — for the primary essence of a vow is when one associates [mitpis] an object with an item forbidden by a vow [davar hanadur], such as when one says: "Behold, this loaf is upon me like consecrated property," and regarding another loaf he says: "Let this be like that one" — this is a vow, as [the Gemara] states in the third chapter of Shevuot (20b): "[One is not liable] unless he vows through an item forbidden by a vow"; and these terms are a form of a vow. And later at the end of our chapter (10a), Reish Lakish says: [Substitutes are] language that the Sages fabricated. And for this reason they instituted substitutes: so that one should not say, "An offering to the Lord," for at times one might say "to the Lord" and not say "an offering," thereby uttering the Name of Heaven in vain. And Rabbi Yochanan says: [They are] foreign languages, for in their language, when they take a vow, they speak this way. And a difficulty arises according to the one who says [they are] foreign languages: Why did [the Mishnah] specify these [particular] terms? Let it say: "In all languages, in whichever language they vow, it shall be a vow!" And the Ri says: Certainly, if it is in their language, it is a vow, provided that they understand [it]; whereas these [terms] of the Mishnah, even if they do not understand this language, it is nevertheless a vow. And according to the one who says [they are] language that the Sages fabricated, a difficulty arises: for so too did the Sages fabricate substitutes for a nazirite, and how could one bring a sacrificial offering on the basis of rabbinic language?! But regarding vows [in general], it is not difficult if one violates [the prohibition of] "you shall not delay" based on rabbinic language. And one can say: That which [Reish Lakish] said, "it is language that they fabricated," was said only with regard to vows, but not with regard to a nazirite. And so it is proven in the Gemara, which challenges: "This is well according to the one who says they are foreign languages; but according to the one who says they are language that the Sages fabricated, what can be said?" But in tractate Nazir, where [the Mishnah] states, "All substitutes for nezirut are like nezirut," [the Gemara] does not raise such a challenge in the Gemara. And the Ri says: This is no proof, for it is common practice [in the Talmud] to elaborate in one place and to be concise in another place; and based on language that the Sages fabricated, one also becomes a nazirite, for since the Sages instituted that one may vow with these terms, it is like primary nezirut, and they have the power to establish their enactment as equivalent to primary nezirut. And furthermore, one can say: Since the Sages instituted these terms, the intent of the one making the vow is toward a full vow, and he resolved in his heart to make it like the primary formulation.

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:1.hebrew: וחרמים כחרמים - תימה: למ"ד סתם חרמים לכהנים, אם ירצה להחרים לבדק הבית, יצטרך לומר "חרם לה'", וא"כ מה הועילו חכמים בתקנתם? והא כל הכנויים אינם אלא משום שלא יזכיר שם שמים לבטלה, שאחרי הכנויים אלו אינו רהוט לומר "לה'", כמו אם יאמר "קרבן" דאז הוא רהוט לומר "לה'". וי"ל, שאם ירצה להחרים לבדק הבית, יאמר "חרם לבדק הבית":
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:1.english: "And dedications are like dedications" - It is puzzling: According to the one who says that unspecified dedications go to the priests, if one wishes to dedicate property to Temple maintenance, he will need to say, "A dedication to the Lord." And if so, what did the Sages achieve by their enactment? For are not all substitute terms instituted only so that one does not mention the Name of Heaven in vain, since after these substitute terms one is not prone to say "to the Lord," as he would be if he were to say "an offering," in which case he is prone to say "to the Lord"? And one can say that if he wishes to dedicate property to Temple maintenance, he can say, "A dedication to Temple maintenance."

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:2.hebrew: ושבועות כשבועות - "שבותה", "שבוקה" — מפרש לקמן. וקשה, דשילהי פ' שבועת העדות (שבועות דף לה) קאמר: "יתן ה' אותך לאלה ולשבועה", נאמר כאן "אלה" ונאמר להלן "אלה" — מה להלן בשם, אף כאן בשם. וכן ריש פ' שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף לח) קאמר: כמאן? כר' חנינא דאמר בעינן שם? אפי' תימא רבנן דאמרי בכינויין, אבל (לא) בלא כינוי דשם לא מחייב. וכן קשה התם, דאמרי' במס' שבועות (דף יט): "שבועה שלא אוכל", "שבועה שאוכל לך" — אסור. ואור״ת: הא דבעינן שם או כינוי — במושבע מפי אחרים; אבל מושבע מפי עצמו — מצי אסר נפשיה בלא שום כינוי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:2.english: "And [substitutes for] oaths are like oaths" - [The terms] shevuta [and] shevuka [the Gemara] explains later [10a]. And it is difficult, as at the end of the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaEdut (Shevuot 35b), [the Gemara] states: "The Lord make you an execration and an oath" (Numbers 5:21) — "execration" is stated here, and "execration" is stated elsewhere; just as elsewhere [it is] with the [divine] Name, so too here [it must be] with the [divine] Name. And similarly, at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaDayanim (Shevuot 38b), [the Gemara] states: In accordance with whose [opinion is this]? In accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina, who says we require the [divine] Name? You may even say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis, who say [an oath may be taken] with appellations [of the divine Name] — but (not) without an appellation of the [divine] Name, one is not liable. And similarly, it is difficult [from that] which we say there, in Tractate Shevuot (19b): "'An oath that I will not eat,' [or] 'An oath that I will eat of yours,' is forbidden." And Rabbeinu Tam says: That which we require the [divine] Name or an appellation [applies only] when one is adjured by others; but one who swears on his own can forbid [the matter to] himself without any appellation.

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:3.hebrew: ונזירות כנזירות - תימה: אמאי לא תנא "איסורי כאיסורי" "והקדשות כהקדשות" וכו'? וי"ל: דלמ"ד "לשון נכרים", לא נמצא להם לשון נכרים אלא בהני דתנא; ולמ"ד "לשון שבדו חכמים", צ"ל דלהכי לא תנא — דלא כתב "ערך לה'", "איסור לה'", "הקדש לה'", כמו דכתיב "חרם לה'" ו"קרבן לה':"
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:2:3.english: "And nazirite vows are like nazirite vows" - It is puzzling: Why did the Mishnah not teach "prohibitions are like prohibitions" and "consecrations are like consecrations," etc.? And one can say that according to the one who says they are foreign languages, no foreign language was found for them except among these that the Mishnah taught; and according to the one who says they are language that the Sages invented, one must say that for this reason the Mishnah did not teach them — for the Torah did not write "an evaluation to the Lord," "a prohibition to the Lord," or "a consecration to the Lord," as it is written: "a dedication to the Lord" and "an offering to the Lord."

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:3:1.hebrew: האומר לחבירו מודר אני ממך - הני ידות מיקרו, שאינו גומר דבריו אלא מתחיל, והוי ידות כמו יד לכלי. ומפרש בגמ' אמאי שבק בכינויין דמיירי בהון, ומפרש ידות דלא איירי בהון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:3:1.english: "One who says to another: I am avowed from you" - These are called intimations [yadot], as he does not finish his statement, but rather begins [it]; and they are [termed] yadot like a handle to a vessel. And it is explained in the Gemara why [the Tanna] set aside substitutes, which he was dealing with, and explains intimations, which he had not been dealing with.

Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:3:2.hebrew: שאני אוכל לך - יש דגורסין ביו"ד: "שאיני אוכל לך". וקשה: דהא אין נדרים חלין אלא על דבר שיש בו ממש! ושמא מיירי דמסרבין בו לאכול, ואומר: "שאיני", והוי כמו "קונם שאני"? — אין. אור"י: דבגמ' משמע דבמידי דמאכל, אף "שאיני" ביו"ד לא קרי בזה דבר שאין בו ממש. ולא דמי לשאיני ישן, דאמר לקמן (נדרים דף יד) [דהוי] דבר שאין בו ממש — דהתם אין בו ממש לא בדבור ולא בשינה; אבל הכא, מ"מ במאכל שהוא מזכיר יש בו ממש, והוא קונם המאכל עצמו ענין זה שאני אוכל. וא"ת: מהו עיקר הנדר? בשלמא חרמים — הוא עיקר מן החרם, ושבועות — מן השבועה; וי"ל שנדר עצמו הוא עיקר, דאמר: "ככר זה עלי נדר", וכן משמע מתני': "כינוי נדרים כנדרים", וקרא נמי מוכח: "כי ידור נדר". ולא נראה: דא"כ, מאי קאמר התם "מודר אני ממך"? אדרבה, הוא עיקר הנדר! ועוד קשה: דקאמר "קונם קונח קונס הרי זה כינוי לקרבן" — הוה ליה למימר "לנדרים"! לכך נראה לפרש: דעיקר הנדר כשהוא אומר "ככר זה עלי קרבן", ו"כי ידור נדר" אתי למימר דבעינן שידור בדבר הנדור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 2a:3:2.english: "That which I eat of yours" - There are some who read [the text] with a yod: "That I will not eat of yours." And this poses a difficulty, for vows take effect only upon an entity that has substance! And perhaps [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case where] they are pressing him to eat, and he says: "[I swear] that I will not [eat]," and it is like [saying]: "Konam [is that] which I [eat]"? — Indeed. The Ri says that in the Gemara it implies that regarding food, even "that I will not [eat]" [spelled] with a yod is not called an entity lacking substance. And it is not comparable to "that I will not sleep," which [the Gemara] states later (Nedarim 14b) [is] an entity lacking substance — for there, there is no substance either in the speech or in the sleep; but here, in any case, in the food that he mentions there is substance, and he renders forbidden [like a] konam the food itself through this matter of what I eat. And if you say: What is the primary [formula of a] vow? Granted, [with regard to] dedicated objects [charamim], the primary [formula] is from [the word] cherem, and [with regard to] oaths, from [the word] shevuah; and one could say that [the word] "neder" itself is the primary [formula], as when one says: "This loaf is upon me [as a] neder," and so the Mishnah implies [in stating]: "Nicknames of vows are like vows," and the verse also proves: "When a man vows a vow" [Numbers 30:3]. However, this does not seem [correct], for if so, why does [the Gemara] say there [that the phrase]: "I am avowed from you" [is an intimation]? On the contrary, that would be the primary [formula of a] vow! And furthermore, it poses a difficulty: since it says: "Konam, konach, konas — these are nicknames for a sacrificial offering [korban]," it should have said: "for vows"! Therefore, it seems [correct] to explain that the primary [formula of a] vow is when one says: "This loaf is upon me [like a] korban," and [the verse] "When a man vows a vow" comes to teach that we require that one vow by [associating the item with] an entity that was [previously] vowed.
